First Week!

My first week at the new job. It's a secretary position, but whatever, as long as it pays the bills. Besides, it looks like interesting things are going on here.
The Doctor says it's best if I don't talk openly with others about his research; I guess he doesn't want anything to leak. A few times I caught myself letting something slip in conversation, it's hard not to brag about something so cool!
I'm not sure why I decided to write this down. The Doctor seems to write everything down. He says it's in case he discovers something important.
Probably why I'm doing it too, I always wanted to be part of something important.
Here's to the new job and to becoming part of something important!

Strange Times...

Things are getting a bit weird here. Only a few weeks after the Doctor's amazing breakthrough, strange visitors started showing up unannounced, asking odd questions about his work.
I knew the Doctor wasn't fond of company, but even he seemed strangely nervous when I told him about the visitors.
He said that from now on we have to keep everything strictly secured, even from the other employees.
He also said something about securing the data, something about hexes. What does that mean? Some kind of curse? The Doctor never struck me as the magic type...
He often uses a lot of big scientific words that I don't really understand, but I kind of like it, it feels like I'm witnessing something great.
I hope everything goes back to normal soon, but I guess that's the price of being part of something important.

Last Day, I Think?

It's officially getting too weird for me.
The visitors come more and more often and they all seem more and more aggressive and nosy. I'm starting to understand why they made the Doctor so nervous, they're starting to scare me too.
Some time ago the Doctor told me to keep this place under strict lockdown and refuse entry to everyone else, including former employees.
But here's the weirdest part.
I haven't seen the Doctor for several days. It's not unusual for him to work in the lab for days on end, but when I looked in there yesterday - he was nowhere to be found! I didn't risk snooping any further, over the last few weeks the Doctor had a habit of leaving the defense systems on.
I think maybe it's time to quit. I can't do much without the boss, and besides, it's getting suspicious. I wanted to be part of something important, but you have to know when to play it safe.
As my dad always used to say: “The wise earn fame, but the prudent survive...”

Robert P.
